projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Deployed on my own server. Every demo opens in one click — no password needed.

warehouse.name: Wirehouse
warehouse.tagline: Stock and cash accounting for a wholesale trader
warehouse.problem: A wholesale food business lives by two questions: what is in stock and what it cost, and where the money is — who owes us, which seller is holding cash, what is left after expenses. All of it in two currencies at once.
warehouse.role: Solo, full stack: Symfony API, Vue client, plus Android build via Capacitor, desktop build via Electron and receipt printing over ESC/POS. 127 test files on the API.
warehouse.challenge: Money is never a float and is never summed across currencies. Sales are allocated over batches FIFO, and four append-only ledgers record every movement — a cancellation appends the opposite row instead of editing history. Every posting path takes pessimistic locks in a fixed order, so two simultaneous requests cannot spend the same cash twice.

smm-crm.name: KH Agency CRM
smm-crm.tagline: Content-planning CRM for an SMM agency
smm-crm.problem: An agency runs dozens of client projects at once; every post has a format, target platforms, a deadline and an executor. Kept in chats, this falls apart: nobody sees today's plan, who is overloaded, or what is overdue.
smm-crm.role: Full stack: Symfony API with real-time updates, Quasar client with kanban boards and a content calendar, three roles, PDF exports and a daily Telegram digest.
smm-crm.challenge: Boards update without polling — Mercure pushes every card move over SSE to all open tabs. Heavy work such as reports and the Telegram digest goes through Messenger to Redis, so the request returns instantly and the job runs in the background.

blender-course.name: Blender course
blender-course.problem: A Blender tutor needed a page that sells the course in Uzbek: what it covers, a showcase of student and author work, pricing plans and a way to enrol.
blender-course.role: Frontend: Quasar single-page app — sections with 3D renders, a YouTube portfolio gallery, pricing and a support form, with i18n.
blender-course.challenge: Layout rather than logic: a dozen YouTube embeds, a Swiper carousel and per-section 3D renders had to stay readable from a wide desktop down to a phone. Built on Quasar's responsive grid, with breakpoint-specific columns on the portfolio and pricing pages.

renthouse.name: Renthouse
renthouse.problem: Owners list cottages, guests search, save favourites and book. Both sides need the same app: a catalogue with photos and a map for guests, a cabinet with their own listings for owners.
renthouse.role: Frontend: Quasar single-page app — catalogue, cottage pages with Google Maps, favourites, owner cabinet with add/edit, auth, profile and i18n.
renthouse.challenge: A three-language interface (Uzbek, Russian, English), a cottage page with the location on Google Maps, and search filters backed by reference dictionaries — regions, districts, amenities, rental terms — each in its own Pinia store so the filters stay consistent across pages.

about.title: About
about.p1: I'm Amirjon, a backend engineer from Uzbekistan. I started writing PHP in 2022 and stayed with it: Symfony and API Platform where the domain matters, Laravel where speed of delivery matters more.
about.p2: What I enjoy most is the part after the code is written — packing a service into a container, giving it a pipeline, metrics and backups, and watching it run without waking anyone at night. I have worked in teams of three to six with Git-flow, code review and a task tracker; on contracts I own the service end to end.
about.p3: Right now I'm looking for a team where I can own services end to end: from the data model to the deployment that ships them.
